items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: Just put me on the record as a writer of these two tunes.

ctx.x: Well, let's get back to the record first, STANLEY (Inaudible). I had -- I didn't have a title to "Dutch Kitchen BOUNCE." I didn't have a title to Go, Red, Go. They were just numbers that we played, and they're my original numbers, because Bootie Woods was with me on Dutch Kitchen BOUNCE, and we wrote that together.

Bob Causer, who was the owner of the Ithaca Hotel in Ithaca, New York, and had a swank eating joint on Cornell University campus called Dutch Kitchen Inn, he came up to my recording session on the first day, and he was a guy who liked, would -- with "St. Vitus Dance," you know. And I was almost -- you know, I was feeling sorry for him, and I was in

bad shape myself. My back was still bothering me, you know, but he wanted -- claim writer and title of these tunes for his situation up there. I said, 'Very good.' He said, 'I don't want no money for it.' He said, 'Just put me on the record as a writer of these two tunes.' He said, 'Now, name this one -- I got the Dutch Kitchen Inn,' and he said, 'You know, Cornell's pep yell is Go, Red, Go.'"
